analysis:
The PR changes only the desktop renderer's model-recommendation UI. It adds per-chip earnings parsing (recommendations.ts chipEarnings/chipRanking, lines 31-77), ranking in recommendedModels (lines 81-96), extended NetworkData typing (contracts.ts), plumbing in StartServing.tsx, AutopilotModels.tsx and RecommendedModels.tsx, and a changelog. It does not touch the provider process, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), keys (A-002/A-003), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009/TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041) or the fan helper.

Checks made:
- chipEarnings validates untrusted coordinator /v1/stats data: it requires networkEarnings freshness, by_chip_window === '24h', Array shape, a safe-integer machines count, and digit-only amount strings before BigInt, so BigInt cannot throw on malformed input. Malformed data returns null and falls back to network totals.
- Rendering uses React text interpolation, so there is no XSS vector. The chip string comes from the local snapshot.
- The recommendation action (recommendedStart) only selects models that are already filtered by model.eligible, which is set by the local runtime. A hostile or compromised coordinator could skew the ranking toward particular models, but that was already possible with the 7-day totals. No privilege or authorization effect results, and serving authorization remains platform-owned.
- Minor correctness note: in the perChip branch of recommendedModels, models whose perChip entry exists have nonzero mean, so the non-null assertion at line 90 is safe.
- A mixed 7d and 24h display is a presentation concern, not a security one.

No security regressions identified. Unverified: the coordinator's actual by_chip publication contract is out of scope and not supplied.
